fixes.explanation: This one is true, friend. Jesus says, "…the one who enters by the gate is the shepherd of the sheep." (John 10:2). The climber from the verse before is the one called a thief and a robber (John 10:1). Then Jesus says the gatekeeper opens the gate for the shepherd (John 10:3).

Jesus doesn't pick out the youngest here. He says the shepherd "…calls his own sheep by name…" (John 10:3). What matters is that they are his own, not how old they are. The word to hold onto is "own."
Jesus says the opposite. About those who came before Him, He says, "…the sheep did not listen to them." (John 10:8). The sheep didn't listen to them. That's the whole answer, friend.
Jesus says, "If anyone enters through Me, he will be saved." (John 10:9). Notice the word "anyone." He goes on to say that person "…will come in and go out and find pasture."

Jesus says, "The man runs away because he is a hired servant and is unconcerned for the sheep." (John 10:13). The sheep aren't his own, and he doesn't care about them. When the wolf shows up, he's gone, and he doesn't look back (John 10:12). That's the big difference between him and the good shepherd.
Jesus doesn't say that. He says, "…I lay down My life in order to take it up again." (John 10:17). The purpose He names is taking it up again. Leaving the flock forever isn't in this verse.

The others say, "These are not the words of a man possessed by a demon. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?" (John 10:21). They point to the opening of blind eyes as their reason. A question like that is hard to argue with.
